name: Senior-Loken Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of nephronophthisis characterized by corticomedullary cystic kidney disease and progressive renal failure
Retinal dystrophy including retinitis pigmentosa or Leber congenital amaurosis leading to visual impairment
Identification of pathogenic variants in known Senior-Loken syndrome-associated genes (e.g., NPHP1, NPHP5/IQCB1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both nephronophthisis and retinal degeneration clinical features; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by genetic testing; renal biopsy may aid in diagnosis

searchTerms: kidney cysts in cortex and medulla
cystic kidney changes in outer and inner layers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Retinal dystrophy (retinitis pigmentosa or Leber congenital amaurosis)

common.symptomName: Polyuria and polydipsia due to impaired renal concentrating ability
Growth retardation secondary to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: growth delay due to chronic kidney disease
poor growth related to kidney problems
high blood pressure due to kidney disease

occasional.symptomName: Anemia related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: low red blood cells due to kidney disease
anemia caused by chronic kidney problems
liver damage causing high blood pressure in portal vein

rare.symptomName: Neurological abnormalities such as cerebellar ataxia
searchTerms: balance and coordination problems from brain

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal failure
Urinalysis showing isosthenuria and mild proteinuria
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing corticomedullary cysts and small echogenic kidneys
Ophthalmologic imaging revealing retinal pigmentary changes and optic nerve pallor
genetic: Pathogenic variants in NPHP1, NPHP5/IQCB1, or other nephronophthisis-associated genes
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating tubulointerstitial fibrosis and tubular basement membrane disruption

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated renal involvement without ocular symptoms
Retinal dystrophy with renal involvement but additional systemic features

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure in a child or adolescent
Early onset visual impairment with retinal dystrophy
Family history of renal disease and blindness
references: Hildebrandt F, Attanasio M, Otto E. Nephronophthisis: disease mechanisms of a ciliopathy. J Am Soc Nephrol. 2009;20(1):23-35.
Otto EA, Helou J, Allen SJ, et al. Nephrocystin-5, a ciliary IQ domain protein, is mutated in Senior-Loken syndrome and interacts with RPGR and calmodulin. Nat Genet. 2005;37(3):282-288.
Wolf MT, Hildebrandt F. Nephronophthisis. Pediatr Nephrol. 2011;26(2):181-194.
